_note: Work done in this archive, in the shape Record Atlas imports. See CLAUDE.md. THREE HONESTIES ABOUT THIS FILE. (1) NO ROW CARRIES A WAYPOINT. Every FamilySearch read below was cited by DGS film number and image ark, which is what this archive has always recorded; the atlas keys on the wc=/owc= waypoint and film numbers have matched it zero times. The waypoints could not be recovered on 29 September because the browser pane was recreated and the FamilySearch session was lost - checked in a second tab and read twice before saying so. The film numbers are in a `film` field and no waypoint has been guessed. WHAT COULD BE ATTACHED INSTEAD: every FamilySearch row now carries a `collection` URL, checked against the atlas's own collections.json by the collection TITLE printed on the record page I opened - so these attach as collection marks even though they cannot attach as volume marks. That is a coarser join than a waypoint and it is not a substitute for one. (2) NOTHING BELOW IS `walked`. Every one of these is a plate opened at a known folio, not a register read entry by entry, and saying otherwise would tell the next person a book is finished when it is not. (3) THIS IS A SWEEP, WHICH THE SKILL DISCOURAGES. The instruction to record as-you-go arrived on 29 September, after the work. Rows from earlier sessions are NOT here - see data/sources-consulted.tsv, which lists 24 films, most of them read before this file existed.

src: FamilySearch / City of Cape Town - South Africa, Cape, Cemetery Records 1872-2011; Maitland (Woltemade) Road Cemetery Record of Interments, Volumes 19 and 21
what: LERENA and TAYLOR interments, Cape Town, across three openings in two volumes - image group 102346234 ('Volume 19', 1946-1947) image 208 of 255, and 102346236 ('Volume 21', 1949-1951) image 93 of 252. THREE PLATES AT KNOWN FOLIOS, NOT A WALK: the registers run to tens of thousands of entries and only the pages carrying these surnames were read. NO WAYPOINT WAS ESTABLISHED - this collection is served as numbered IMAGE GROUPS and no wc=/owc= appeared in any URL on the path from the record to the plate, so the image-group numbers are recorded in `film` and nothing has been guessed. THE SURNAME IS WHY THIS NEARLY FAILED: the 1950 burial is indexed as LESINA, and no surname search of any spelling reaches it. It was found by searching GIVEN NAME plus death year within the collection and reading 663 results. That technique is the transferable part. ONE DEFECT WORTH PASSING ON: FamilySearch's own generated citation for image group 102346236 reads 'Maitland, Cape Town, Cape, Cape Colony, Seine-Maritime, France records' - its place matcher resolves this Cape Colony to a French department.

src: FreeREG - Northam (St Margaret) and Bideford, Devon: parish register coverage checked before searching
what: TAYLOR baptisms, Northam and Bideford, 1869-1891, for a daughter born 1882. NOTHING, AND THE NULL IS FULLY EXPLAINED RATHER THAN MERELY RECORDED. FreeREG's own contents pages give Northam, St Margaret, Parish Register: 12,120 records, FIRST 1653, LAST 1817 - the coverage stops sixty-five years before the record wanted. Bideford is listed as a place and has NO church, NO register and NO records at all. So this is a coverage wall, not an absent baptism, and nobody should read the zero as evidence about the family. THE SEARCH WAS RUN ANYWAY, with a control first: surname TAYLOR alone, Northam, 1869-1891, returned 0, which the contents page then explained.

src: findmypast - Devon Baptisms (South West Heritage Trust; transcribed by Devon FHS volunteers); Northam St Margaret, archive reference 1843A/PR/1/16
what: TAYLOR baptisms at Northam, Devon, 1874-1889. SEVEN CHILDREN OF ONE COUPLE RECOVERED IN A SINGLE QUERY, by searching on the MOTHER's forenames rather than each child's - which is the transferable method here, because it is what makes an ABSENCE provable rather than merely unfound. A CONTROL WAS RUN FIRST on the one child whose birth date and address this archive already held, and it returned. ALSO A CONTROLLED NEGATIVE: the candidate tenth child this archive had graded STRONG is not in the series, and the only two same-name baptisms in the county near the date belong to two other men of the same name, identified by their wives' forenames. The candidate was downgraded on the strength of it.

src: General Register Office (gro.gov.uk) - the GRO's own online birth index for England and Wales
what: TAYLOR births with mother's maiden surname BRAYLEY, Bideford district, 1870-1893. TEN SEARCHES - five year-windows times two sexes, because sex is a mandatory field and the year range is capped at plus or minus two. NINE CHILDREN OF ONE COUPLE RECOVERED, AND A TENTH DISPROVED. THE POINT OF THIS SOURCE, which no free index can match: the GRO's own index PRINTS THE MOTHER'S MAIDEN SURNAME on every birth from 1837, so a search on father's surname plus mother's maiden name returns a couple's children BY DEFINITION rather than by inference. FreeBMD carries no mother's maiden name in its birth index and never will, which is why three weeks of candidate-weighing there could not settle what this settled in ten searches. THE CRITICAL WINDOW WAS RE-RUN ON 'SIMILAR SOUNDING VARIATIONS' because a spelling variant of the mother's surname was documented in an earlier census: 28 births across England, the same two in the district. IT NEEDS AN ACCOUNT, which the archive owner signed in; this session does not create accounts.

src: General Register Office (gro.gov.uk) - birth index, England and Wales; second pass, one generation up
what: BRAYLEY births (loose surname matching) with mother's maiden surname TEMPLE, 1838-1852, both sexes - six searches. TWO CHILDREN FOUND AND TWO ABSENCES ESTABLISHED. The method is the same as the pass before it and the lesson is sharper: searching for a PERSON who may never have been registered can only ever fail, while searching for her PARENTS returns the children who ARE in the book and therefore the shape of who is missing. THE SPELLING CONTROL IS BUILT IN - the query used one spelling of the surname and the index returned the other both times, so the absences are not an artefact. WHAT THE ABSENCES MEAN: the two earliest children, both born in a capital city in the early 1840s, are unregistered; the two later ones are registered. Birth registration was not compulsory on parents in England and Wales until the Act of 1874, in force 1875, and under-registration in the 1840s fell heaviest on the urban poor - which this household is recorded as being. Useful to anyone hunting an early-Victorian birth that will not appear.

src: FamilySearch - South Africa, Transvaal Civil Death 1869-1954 and Orange Free State Civil Death Registration 1902-1954
what: LERENA across the whole of South Africa - 413 results, every one read for an indexed PARENT. EXACTLY THREE CARRY ONE and all three are infant children of one man, none of whom appears on his own death notice because a death notice lists the living. TWO METHOD NOTES WORTH PASSING ON. (1) A DATE FILTER PRODUCED A SILENT FALSE ZERO: the same surname-plus-country query returned 0 with a date range attached and 413 without it, and nothing in the result said the filter had misfired. (2) AN AGE FIELD IN BOTH COLLECTIONS IS A DEFAULT, NOT A MEASUREMENT: two infants a decade apart are both given 'Age: 0 days', while two independent family dates give them five days and four. Two errors in the same direction is an unfilled form field. The age was discarded rather than used to correct the dates.

src: FamilySearch FULL-TEXT SEARCH - the words on unindexed images, not an index of names
what: LERENA and the exact phrase 'Juan Carlos Lerena', tested as a ROUTE rather than worked as a search. THE POINT FOR ANY ARCHIVE: full text goes round the transcriber, so it reaches a man with a COMPOUND SURNAME who is filed under his father's name and is invisible to a search for his mother's. One such man was found in two hits across the whole corpus and correctly set aside on the surname order. WHAT THE CORPUS HOLDS FOR THE RIVER PLATE: Arquidiocesis de Montevideo MARRIAGE DISPENSATION RECORDS 1856-1932 - a class that names a groom's parents; Flores and Trinidad baptisms and deaths; Montevideo burial registers 1886-2021; Catedral baptisms and deaths. AND THE HOLE: SOUTH AFRICA IS NOT IN IT. A full-text search with a South African place filter errors outright and no South African collection surfaces unfiltered, so a Cape question gains nothing here. Recorded as a route confirmed and not yet worked.

src: FamilySearch FULL-TEXT - Flores (Uruguay). Civil Birth Records 1916-1925, act No. 10 of 1922
what: The 1913 marriage dispensation of a PELAEZ groom and a LERENA bride named a degree of kinship and no parents. METHOD, AND IT IS THE TRANSFERABLE PART: search the full text for the BRIDE by exact phrase, then look for a CHILD'S BIRTH ACT rather than for the marriage - because a Uruguayan civil birth act names BOTH PARENTS AND ALL FOUR GRANDPARENTS with their ages, trades and addresses. One act answered the dispensation outright and gave five adults their first recorded birth year.
note: NO WAYPOINT ESTABLISHED. A full-text image ark carries no wc=/owc= parameter, so the DGS film number is recorded instead and the waypoint is left null rather than guessed from a similar volume. Film 008165367, item 6, image 195 - read directly off the page, not inferred. CAUTION WORTH CARRYING: the AI transcript renders one clerk's single letterform as SERENA in one line and LERENA four lines later; the plate shows both are L. Read the plate before recording a surname from this corpus.

src: FamilySearch FULL-TEXT - Santisima Trinidad, Trinidad, Flores (Uruguay). Baptism Records August 1905-August 1909
what: The same method against the 1894 dispensation. A Trinidad baptism act of this period names BOTH PAIRS OF GRANDPARENTS in a single line ('Abuelos paternos: X y Y. Maternos: Z y W'), which makes a parish register do the work of a civil birth act. The child's baptism named the parents of both halves of the couple, merged two register rows this archive had split the same morning, and added a sixth child to a founding couple.
note: NO WAYPOINT ESTABLISHED - film number recorded instead, not guessed. Film 008163893, item 5, image 20, read off the page. THE FILM NUMBER WAS WRONG HERE FOR AN HOUR: it was carried across from the 1889-1894 book (008164291) on the assumption that two volumes of one parish share a film. They do not. Checked against the page and corrected before anything was committed. ALSO A FALSE ZERO: this page first returned 'Unable to load the data - taking longer than expected', which reads as a record containing nothing; its own REFRESH button returned the find of the day.

src: FamilySearch FULL-TEXT - Santisima Trinidad, Trinidad, Flores (Uruguay). Baptism Records 1889-1894
what: Searched the exact phrase 'Eduviges Pelaez' across the whole full-text corpus. CORPUS SHAPE WORTH KNOWING: the phrase returns seven pages dominated by COLOMBIA and GUATEMALA, with two Uruguayan hits on page one - so a quoted two-word phrase is usable but still needs the in-page Place facet. Found the bride of the 1894 dispensation standing PROXY GODMOTHER at Trinidad on 1 April 1894, the day after her dispensation was granted at Montevideo. No parents here; the yield was placing her in the parish.
note: NO WAYPOINT ESTABLISHED - film 008164291, item 2, recorded instead. FOR ANY ARCHIVE USING THIS SEARCH: a place written into the URL as f.recordCountry errors outright with 'Something Went Wrong'. Confirmed today for URUGUAY, having been recorded yesterday for SOUTH AFRICA - so the broken thing is the PARAMETER, not the country. Use the Place facet inside the page.

src: FamilySearch FULL-TEXT - Arquidiocesis de Montevideo, Marriage Dispensation Records, the volumes of the 1850s (1852-1855, 1855-1857, 1857-1860)
what: THE FINDING ANY ARCHIVE USING THIS COLLECTION NEEDS: it is not one record class, it is two, and the difference is the DECADE. The volumes of 1885-1913 are the Vicar General's SUMMARY LEDGER - one sentence per couple, naming no parents. The volumes of the 1850s in the SAME collection are FULL EXPEDIENTES: petition, numbered interrogatory, sworn witness depositions naming the PARENTS AND GRANDPARENTS of both parties, the Cura Vicario's report, and sometimes a KINSHIP DIAGRAM the priest drew himself. Three were read (Dec 1854, Aug 1855, Feb 1858) and all three name four generations. This archive had published twice that these records cannot name parents; both statements were generalisations from one date range.
note: NO WAYPOINT ESTABLISHED and no DGS film number is shown on these full-text pages, so both fields are left null rather than guessed; the image arks are in the url and in data/sources-consulted.tsv. HOW THEY WERE FOUND: full-text search on the exact phrase of a BRIDE's name and then a FATHER's name - 'Socorro Lerena', 'Alejandro Lerena'. READ THE PLATE: the transcripts render one clerk's single letterform as Serena, Lorena, Leresa and Lerena on ONE page.

src: FamilySearch FULL-TEXT - Flores (Uruguay). Civil Death Records 1888-1917
what: Read for its GRANDPARENTS rather than its subject. A Uruguayan civil death act of this period names the deceased's parents and all four grandparents, which makes a death register a pedigree source for people who died long before it. One act placed three families at once. CAUTION RECORDED: no birth years were taken from the stated ages, because the act's own date was not read - only the book's range - and an age without a date is not a birth year.
note: NO WAYPOINT - full-text image ark only, recorded in the url. Found by the exact phrase 'Alejandro Lerena'.

src: FamilySearch FULL-TEXT - Santisima Trinidad, Trinidad, Flores (Uruguay). Baptism Records 1848-1857
what: Searched the exact phrase 'Socorro Lerena'. The parish is called 'la Santisima Trinidad de los PORONGOS' in its own register at this date, which is the town's older name and is worth knowing before searching for it. The hit was a GODMOTHER rather than a parent - which still dated a woman to the parish six years before her marriage and gave her full baptismal name. A godparent line is evidence and this archive counts it.
pages: unrecorded - single opening reached from a search result
note: NO WAYPOINT - full-text image ark only. The baptism format in this book names PARENTS and GODPARENTS but NOT grandparents; the grandparent format appears in the same parish by 1905. Worth knowing before opening a book of this series expecting four generations.

src: FamilySearch - Catedral Basilica San Jose, San Jose de Mayo (Uruguay). Religious Marriage Records March 1825-September 1859
what: Reached from an INDEX entry rather than by searching: the 'Uruguay, Marriages, 1840-1900' index record carries Digital Folder, Microfilm and Image numbers under 'Document Information', which is the cheapest route from an index hit to the plate and is worth knowing. Image 87 is the marriage of 3 February 1837. THE POINT FOR ANY ARCHIVE: reading the plate CORRECTED the argument it was opened to confirm. A claim had been published that this act and another document give the same place of origin; the act says COLLA where the other says SAN JOSE - and the index field 'Birthplace: Colla' had said so all along, on the very page being cited.
note: NO WAYPOINT ESTABLISHED. This was reached by film number, and a film page's wc= names only its default segment - so the film number is recorded and the waypoint left null rather than guessed. THE VOLUME'S YEAR RANGE WAS CHECKED AGAINST THE FRAME BEFORE RECORDING: the book is March 1825 - September 1859 and the act is 1837, so the range contains it. Microfilm 625330; the index entry giving the locator is ark 1:1:F21B-SZ5.

src: FamilySearch FULL-TEXT - Flores (Uruguay). Civil Birth Records 1887-1902, and San Jose de Mayo Religious Death Records 1839-1851
what: Searched the exact phrase of a GRANDMOTHER's name - 'Casimira Montano' - rather than any of her descendants. ACROSS THE WHOLE CORPUS IT RETURNS 123 HITS AND ONLY TWO ARE URUGUAYAN, which is what a distinctive married-surname pair does: almost no noise, and the two hits are both the right family. One was a birth act naming her as a grandmother with her age, widowhood and STREET ADDRESS; the other, in the San Jose burial register, a daughter of hers dead at seven days in 1850. The birth act merged two register rows that had been correctly held apart for eighteen days.
note: NO WAYPOINT - full-text image arks only, recorded in the url and in data/sources-consulted.tsv. San Jose burials: ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS27-J7GH-Y. A HAZARD WORTH CARRYING ACROSS ARCHIVES: the infant buried in 1850 bears her grandmother's forename, and a later woman of that same forename is listed elsewhere as a candidate child of the same couple. Reusing a dead infant's name was ordinary practice and is a standing duplicate hazard in any family that did it.
